items.title: Identificação humana por meio da odontologia forense em casos de desastres em massa
items.abstract: Introduction: Mass casualty incidents, whether of natural or human origin, result in a high number of fatalities, often under conditions that render visual identification impossible. In this context, forensic dentistry stands out as a primary method for human identification, in accordance with the INTERPOL Disaster Victim Identification (DVI) protocol. Objective: To analyze the importance of the main human identification techniques used in forensic dentistry during mass casualty incidents, as well as the challenges encountered in their application. Methodology: This is a literature review conducted by searching the SciELO, PubMed, LILACS, and Google Scholar databases, using descriptors such as "forensic dentistry," "human identification," "identification techniques," and "dental arch," covering publications from 2016 to 2026. Results: The 20 studies analyzed showed that the comparison of antemortem and postmortem records, imaging exams (CBCT, intraoral scanning), and the analysis of anatomical characteristics and prostheses are the most widely used resources. The quality of dental records proved to be the main limiting factor, with reports of documentation failures, absence of complete odontograms, and lack of standardization. Digital technologies and artificial intelligence showed promising results, but still require validation in real-world scenarios. Conclusion: Forensic dentistry is essential for human identification in mass disasters, especially due to the resistance of teeth and the possibility of comparison with previous records. However, the effectiveness of the method depends on the quality and standardization of dental records, integration among multidisciplinary teams, and scientific validation of new technologies.

items.title: Identification and Analysis of Coal Mine Accident Risk Factors: A Bayesian Network Approach Using Association Rules and Expert-Validated LLM-Generated Directional Priors
items.abstract: Although coal-mine accident reports contain intertwined risk factors, co-occurrence alone cannot establish causal direction or quantify the risk of accident occurrence. The symmetry of statistical co-occurrence and the potential asymmetry of conditional relationships highlight the difficulty of determining meaningful directions between risk factors. This study aims to identify factors associated with severity in reported coal-mine accidents and examine their conditional dependencies. Based on a sample of 800 accident investigation reports collected from 2010 to 2025, this study integrated text mining and expert review to extract and standardize 55 risk factors. Subsequently, the Apriori algorithm was employed to mine candidate associations, and expert prior knowledge was introduced to establish directional constraints, forming the basis for constructing a Bayesian network. The analysis extracted 274 association rules and constructed a network topology comprising 57 nodes and 187 directed edges. The comprehensive assessment revealed that factors such as ventilation, roof management, safety education and training, employee safety awareness, and gas accumulation have particularly significant impacts on accident severity. This study not only provides a quantitative, structured analytical framework for deconstructing the causes of complex accidents but also offers a scientific basis for coal mining enterprises to transition their safety management from passive post-event response to proactive, targeted pre-event control. It holds significant practical value for optimizing the allocation of safety resources and enhancing the intrinsic safety level of coal mines.

items.title: Implicit Algorithm Aversion: How Consumer Characteristics Shape Perceptions of Ads Designed by Undisclosed AI Versus Human Advertising Professionals
items.abstract: The emergence of generative artificial intelligence (AI) has profoundly reshaped the marketing landscape, providing scalable efficiencies in ad creation. However, the consumer side of AI integration remains underexplored. Drawing on algorithm aversion theory, this research extends the literature by examining how consumer characteristics moderate the persuasive impact of AI- and human-designed ads. Across a pretest and six large-scale experimental studies involving 6,579 consumer evaluations in Japan, this research finds that advertisements with undisclosed AI authorship often outperform human-designed advertisements in enhancing ad perceptions of creativity, credibility, clarity, and mental imagery (i.e., stimulating vivid consumer imagination) and, consequently, increasing purchase intentions. However, AI-generated ads are less effective among consumers with more generative AI experience, higher education, greater product category involvement, and lower interest in science. In these consumer segments, human-designed ads often have the advantage. These findings extend algorithm aversion theory by providing indirect evidence consistent with an implicit mechanism through which consumer characteristics trigger implicit algorithm detection (i.e., sensing algorithmic markers) and implicit algorithm aversion (i.e., subconscious devaluation of perceived artificiality) without requiring explicit disclosure of AI authorship. The findings inform marketing practice by emphasizing the importance of consumer segmentation.

items.title: IMPROVING ENGLISH LANGUAGE TEACHING THROUGH THE INTEGRATION OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND DIGITAL EDUCATIONAL TECHNOLOGIES: PROFESSIONAL COMPETENCIES OF THE 21ST-CENTURY TEACHER AND THE OPPORTUNITIES OF HYBRID LEARNING
items.abstract: This article examines the integration of artificial intelligence and digital educational technologies into English language teaching within the global educational ecosystem. It analyzes the development of the professional and technological competencies of 21st-century teachers, the potential of computational linguistics in language education, and the pedagogical and psychological aspects of hybrid and distance learning. In contemporary education, the use of artificial intelligence-based tools plays an important role in addressing learners’ individual needs, developing language skills, enhancing learning motivation, and organizing the educational process effectively. At the same time, the application of digital technologies should be combined with teachers’ methodological expertise, critical thinking, information literacy, and pedagogical responsibility. Based on a theoretical and analytical approach, the article explores the pedagogical opportunities of integrating artificial intelligence tools into English language lessons, identifies existing challenges, and provides practical recommendations.

items.title: Incorporación de la temática de inteligencia artificial en programas de formación docente en Uruguay
items.abstract: The popularization of agents, models, and tools incorporating artificial intelligence is a phenomenon that has recently mobilized social and educational spheres due to new ethical and academic considerations, as well as the difficulties that arise when designing and evaluating learning experiences. The purpose of this study was to characterize the meaning and assess the scope of references to Artificial Intelligence (AI) in teacher training programs for secondary education in Uruguay, within the current curriculum (Plan 2023). The study focuses on STEM-related specialties. Through a content analysis of 156 curricular documents, the context of AI references was quantified and interpreted. The results show that these references are given a more instrumental than critical meaning. The presence of the Computer Science Teacher Training specialty is relevant, given that the interdisciplinary nature of the STEM approach can contribute to deepening critical thinking, transversality, and curricular flexibility for the pedagogical inclusion of these emerging technologies in teacher training.

items.title: Índices de burnout entre profissionais de enfermagem: revisão narrativa da literatura publicada entre 2022 e 2026.
items.abstract: Objective: To examine burnout rates among nursing professionals reported in publications from 2022 to 2026, considering measurement differences, associated factors, and implications for care. Methods: A descriptive narrative literature review based on scientific studies and reviews published within the defined period. Results: A 2023 meta-analysis estimated a global burnout prevalence of 30.0% (95% CI: 26.0–34.0%). A 2025 umbrella review reported a pooled prevalence of 33.45% for emotional exhaustion, 25.0% for depersonalization, and 33.49% for reduced personal accomplishment. A Brazilian study published in 2026 involving 3,594 nursing workers identified moderate exhaustion in 42.29% of participants; this indicator should not be interpreted as an overall syndrome prevalence. Conclusion: Burnout is a major occupational health concern, and heterogeneous measurement approaches require cautious interpretation and organizational prevention.

items.title: Inequalities in the Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence and Barriers to Adoption: Evidence from Household Survey Data
items.abstract: This paper examines the socioeconomic, demographic, digital, and labour-market factors associated with Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) adoption and the barriers that prevent its use. Using nationally representative data for Spain from the 2025 Survey on Equipment and Use of ICT in Households, we distinguish between private, work-related, and educational uses of GAI and analyse the heterogeneous reasons for non-adoption. To account for the selective observation of barriers among non-users, we estimate a multivariate sample-selection model with valid exclusion restrictions. The results reveal significant inequalities in both GAI adoption and non-adoption barriers. GAI adoption is positively associated with human capital, digital resources, and technology-intensive work environments. Moreover, non-adoption barriers vary substantially across population groups, with older, less educated, and female individuals facing primarily skill- and information-related constraints, while more educated and digitally connected individuals are more likely to question the relevance of these technologies. The findings suggest that the emerging GAI divide reflects both traditional forms of digital inequality and heterogeneous informational, capability-related, and attitudinal barriers. Policies aimed at promoting inclusive GAI adoption should therefore combine digital-skills development, awareness-raising initiatives, and measures to strengthen trust in AI technologies.

items.title: Influence of Mathematics Anxiety and Level of Motivation on the Academic Achievement of Public Senior High School Students
items.abstract: Mathematics anxiety and motivation shape how senior high school students engage with mathematics, but their joint influence on achievement has received limited attention in Philippine public schools. Grounded in the Integrated Cognitive-Emotional Theory and Self-Determination Theory, this descriptive-correlational study examined the influence of mathematics anxiety and motivation level on the academic achievement of 109 Grade 11 and 12 students at General Santos City National High School in School Year 2025–2026. Anxiety was measured in four dimensions with an instrument adapted from the Abbreviated Math Anxiety Scale, motivation in three dimensions with items adapted from the Academic Motivation Scale (α = .78 to .85), and achievement through first- and second-quarter mathematics grades. Chi-square and Pearson correlation were applied. Anxiety was High in all dimensions, with emotional and cognitive anxiety highest (M = 3.23). Students’ motivation was predominantly extrinsic (M = 3.30, Very High), followed by intrinsic motivation (M = 3.23, High), with amotivation Fair (M = 2.28). Achievement was Satisfactory and improved from 83.45 to 84.20. Age, sex, grade level, strand, and family income were associated with anxiety and motivation, while sex, grade level, and strand were associated with achievement. Anxiety was negatively related to achievement (r = −.42, p = .001), and motivation was positively related to it (r = .38, p = .002). The results are consistent with a model in which anxiety drains cognitive resources during evaluation while motivation sustains effort. A school mental health plan focusing on regulation at the point of performance, autonomous motivation, and family engagement is proposed.

items.title: Institutionalising Practicum Modules in Tanzania’s Livestock Training System: Institutional Challenges and Implications for Competency-Based Education and Training
items.abstract: Competency-based education and training (CBET) requires graduates to apply knowledge, perform occupational tasks, solve practical problems, and exercise professional judgement in authentic work environments. This narrative review examined the meaning and educational significance of practicum, the relationship between classroom learning and workplace competence, potential implementation barriers, relevant international experiences, and strategies for strengthening practicum in Tanzania’s livestock training system. The review synthesised literature and documentary information on workplace learning, agricultural and technical training, and apprenticeship approaches in Tanzania and selected countries. The findings distinguish theoretical instruction, institution-based practical training, field activities, and structured workplace practicum as complementary but non-equivalent learning experiences. Effective practicum requires clearly defined learning outcomes, authentic occupational tasks, supervised participation, constructive feedback, documented learning, and competency-based assessment. The synthesis identified potential implementation barriers, including inadequate financing, limited placement opportunities, unclear institutional and employer responsibilities, insufficient supervisor preparation, safety and safeguarding concerns, and weak assessment arrangements. International and Tanzanian apprenticeship examples highlighted transferable principles of employer engagement, shared training responsibilities, structured supervision, and quality assurance. However, available evidence does not establish the prevalence of these barriers or the adequacy of practicum across all Tanzanian livestock training institutions. The review proposes a coordinated framework integrating curriculum alignment, approved placement hosts, progressive competency development, student protection, sustainable financing, employer partnerships, and continuous monitoring. Tanzania should establish context-sensitive practicum standards, assess institutional readiness, strengthen collaboration between training institutions and livestock-sector employers, and pilot and evaluate implementation before wider adoption. National empirical research is also needed to establish baseline conditions and assess practicum quality and outcomes. Institutionalising structured practicum could strengthen the relevance of livestock education and support graduate preparedness for employment

items.title: INTEGRATING ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND DIGITAL TECHNOLOGIES IN LANGUAGE TEACHING: A PEDAGOGICAL REVIEW
items.abstract: This paper examines the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) and digital technologies into language teaching. It explores their role in developing vocabulary, grammar, pronunciation, writing, and independent learning. The study adopts a literature review approach and uses the SAMR model to discuss technology integration in education. It also highlights challenges such as the reliability of AI-generated feedback, learners’ dependence on AI tools, and unequal access to digital resources. The paper emphasizes that effective technology integration requires clear learning objectives, teacher guidance, and meaningful communication. It concludes that AI and digital technologies should complement, rather than replace, teachers in language education.

items.title: INTEGRATING ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND DIGITAL TECHNOLOGIES TO DEVELOP ESP STUDENTS' READING COMPETENCE THROUGH SPECIALIZED TEXTS
items.abstract: This article examines how artificial intelligence (AI) and digital technologies can be integrated into English for Specific Purposes (ESP) reading instruction using discipline-specific texts. The problem addressed is the mismatch between the linguistic and conceptual demands of authentic professional materials and learners’ varying levels of reading proficiency. A qualitative, literature-based methodological design was employed, combining thematic synthesis of established ESP and reading scholarship with instructional design analysis. The principal result is a three-stage framework linking pre-reading preparation, guided while-reading analysis and post-reading transfer to specific AI-supported teacher actions and observable learning evidence. A worked example demonstrates implementation with a professional text and identifies safeguards for accuracy, privacy and learner autonomy. The framework is a proposed pedagogical model, not an experimentally validated intervention. The article concludes that AI is most useful when it supports purposeful reading, disciplinary meaning-making and teacher-led formative assessment rather than replacing authentic engagement with texts.

items.title: Integrating artificial intelligence and multi-omics with systems and network pharmacology for drug repurposing
items.abstract: Developing a new medicine can cost two to three billion US dollars over ten to 17 years, and roughly nine of ten compounds entering first-in-human testing never reach regulatory approval. Drug repurposing can reuse existing pharmacological and safety information, although a new indication may require additional toxicology, formulation, dose or pharmacokinetic studies. This narrative review examines how artificial intelligence, computational pharmacology, network and systems pharmacology, multi-omics and polypharmacology inform repurposing hypotheses. We distinguish disease-first, drug-first, phenotype-first and patient-stratification approaches and qualitatively assess the evidence supporting individual candidates. The methods covered include drug-target and drug-disease prediction, virtual screening, molecular dynamics, free-energy estimation, off-target and toxicity prediction, network analysis, and perturbation-signature integration. These methods contribute complementary information and can be applied iteratively rather than in a fixed sequence. Network proximity, signature reversal and observational associations nominate candidates; experimental target engagement, causal mechanism and clinical efficacy require distinct evidence. Positive and negative clinical examples illustrate this distinction, while preprints are identified separately from peer-reviewed studies. Integration remains constrained by dataset bias, incomplete interactomes, limited transferability and external validation, alongside exposure, experimental, funding and regulatory challenges. Computational integration is making repurposing increasingly hypothesis-driven, but prospective clinical validation remains limited. Its translational value depends on reliable predictions and independent, indication-specific experimental and clinical evaluation.

items.title: Integrating Artificial Intelligence into Soft Skills Development: Opportunities and Challenges
items.abstract: In the 21st century, soft skills such as communication, critical thinking, teamwork, leadership, problem-solving, and emotional intelligence are essential for personal and professional development. Unlike academic knowledge, they enhance the practical impact of what a person knows. As artificial intelligence (AI) develops rapidly, integrating it into education, and specifically into soft skills development, may accelerate learning. However, few existing solutions bring these skills together in a single system. Many learners prioritize academic knowledge because soft skills are not formally assessed and do not lead to a diploma. As a result, these skills are often neglected, although employers increasingly expect them in both international and domestic settings. This article explores how soft skills development can be combined in a single AI-based system. The pilot study draws on a survey of some respondents. The analysis examines how respondents currently use AI to develop soft skills, which skills they consider the most important and the most difficult to develop, and whether attitudes differ by age or occupation.

items.title: Integrating Foreign Students Through Education for Values
items.abstract: Recognising the challenges that international students face in integrating the Portuguese Education System, NOVA University launched a semester-long Foundation Program in 2017. Within this program, we introduced the Ideas Club course in 2020 to promote students’ engagement and facilitate long-term academic success. This paper examines whether and how the course has helped these students overcome cultural barriers and adapt to the European context. European issues serve as a guiding framework to help non-European students interact and discuss in constructive ways, thereby grasping the complexities of European reality. The course adopts a dialogic pedagogical approach, promoting student-led discussions on diverse topics while encouraging consciousness, critical reflection, and the dismantling of some stereotypes. Literature in international foundation education highlights the importance of self-determination theory in fostering intrinsic motivation, which is essential for the desired engagement and academic success. We show in this paper how the Ideas Club contributes to fostering intrinsic motivation.

items.title: Intelligent chemical production mode occupational health risk identification, assessment and intervention study
items.abstract: The intelligent transformation of the chemical industry has reshaped petrochemical production workflows and altered occupational-health risk landscapes. This paper delineates four typical operating scenarios for intelligent chemical manufacturing and develops a four-tier hierarchical risk indicator system covering objectives, criteria, factors, and measurable indicators. A hybrid entropy-weighted Bayesian-network evaluation model is established, where entropy weights calibrate prior probabilities of root-node inputs while conditional-probability tables are retained to characterize risk-coupling behaviors. Model performance is validated via time-series partitioning, multi-model benchmark comparisons, and cross-validation using Monte-Carlo simulations. An entropy-weighted TOPSIS multi-criteria decision-making method is adopted to rank intervention-target priorities, and discrete time-series analysis quantifies outcomes from a six-month closed-loop intervention program. Results demonstrate that human-machine interaction, psychological, and managerial risks dominate occupational-health hazards within intelligent chemical-production contexts. Three highly sensitive critical drivers are identified: operating-instruction error rate, risk-monitoring gap duration, and information-overload frequency. Multi-criteria decision analysis further reveals that high-sensitivity risk factors do not inherently represent optimal intervention targets. The proposed model achieves 88.2% prediction accuracy on time-series test datasets, and statistically significant overall-risk reduction is observed post-intervention. This work offers theoretical support for risk identification, equipment retrofitting, and worker-health protection for smart petrochemical sites, facilitating the synergistic advancement of chemical-industry intelligent modernization, operational safety, and employee occupational-health outcomes.

items.title: Intelligent Orchestration for Automated Attack Surface Management: A Comprehensive Survey of AI Agents, Adaptive Security Assessment, and Vulnerability Discovery
items.abstract: Attack surface management (ASM) is moving from periodic, tool-centric scanning towards continuous, intelligence-driven assessment. This survey reviews 31 curated sources (2021–2026) covering autonomous penetration testing, LLM-based security agents, multi-agent architectures, reinforcement-learning (RL) planners, security-tool orchestration, attack-path analysis, vulnerability validation, and evaluation benchmarks. Each source was coded against a common schema (AI technique, agent architecture, event-driven support, adaptive tool selection, fallback, validation, attack-chain coverage, testbed, metrics, findings, limitations). We present a literature matrix, comparative tables, a taxonomy, and a gap analysis. Within the reviewed corpus, the literature is strong on agent reasoning and planning but documents few complete implementations of event-driven orchestration, quality-aware tool fallback, and systematic false-positive-reducing validation within a single evaluated framework. Evaluation is also fragmented across simulations, CTF-style benchmarks, and small vulnerable testbeds. FoundFirst AI, the authors’ AI-powered ASM project, is used only as practical motivation. This survey reports no new experimental results. Keywords—attack surface management, penetration testing, large language models, multi-agent systems, security orchestration, vulnerability validation, reinforcement learning, event-driven architecture.

items.title: Interactive Multimedia Game-Based Learning (MMI-GBL) to Support Student Engagement and Problem Solving in Elementary Education: A Systematic Literature Review
items.abstract: Background: Interactive multimedia and educational games offer opportunities for elementary learning, but their mechanisms and outcome measures are heterogeneous.Aims: To synthesize the design features of interactive multimedia game-based learning (MMI-GBL), the evidence on student engagement, the implications for problem solving, and the methodological limitations of the field.Methods: This systematic literature review follows PRISMA 2020 reporting principles with descriptive mapping and narrative synthesis. A previously compiled 41-reference bibliography was reconciled into a retrospectively defined core set of 17 publications (2022–2026) and 24 supporting references. Core sources comprise seven empirical studies and ten secondary syntheses. Data were entered into a structured extraction matrix and appraised qualitatively by context and outcome construct.Results: Five empirical publications concern elementary or early elementary learners, including one complementary multimedia study, and address mathematics learning, task solving, computing terminology, and engagement. Recurring design features include coherent multimedia representations, explicit goals and missions, adaptive scaffolding, specific feedback, and opportunities to retry and reflect. Designs in which scaffolding and feedback prompted learners to choose strategies, explain, and revise were associated with learning and engagement gains, whereas rewards detached from reasoning contributed little. Behavioral and cognitive engagement were the dimensions most often evidenced; emotional and agentic engagement were rarely measured. Perceived usefulness or achievement does not directly measure problem-solving performance, and external meta-analytic estimates remain contextual.Conclusion: MMI-GBL is most effective when multimedia features, game mechanics, scaffolding, feedback, and teacher facilitation are aligned with meaningful learning activities. Further elementary-level research is needed to strengthen evidence on engagement and problem-solving outcomes.

items.title: Interpelar para engajar: perguntas em práticas discursivas no Instagram e no Facebook
items.abstract: This article analyzes the discursive functioning of questions in Instagram and Facebook posts, understood as a strategy for interpellating the interlocutor and generating engagement on social media. Grounded in Applied Linguistics, Discourse Analysis, and literacy studies, it draws on authors such as Benveniste, Bakhtin and Volochinov, Pêcheux, Orlandi, Kerbrat-Orecchioni, Maingueneau, Charaudeau, Paveau, Bucher and Helmond, Gerlitz and Helmond, Recuero, and Duffy and Chan, among others, to understand the question as an enunciative-discursive practice crossed by specific sociotechnical conditions. Adopting a qualitative, descriptive-interpretative approach, the study analyzes a corpus of twelve interrogative statements — six from Instagram and six from Facebook — collected between June and September of the current year through an exemplary, rather than statistical, sampling. The analysis shows that questions circulating on these platforms tend to organize themselves between two poles: genuinely interpellative questions, which constitute the interlocutor as a subject called upon to take a stance amid a conflict of meaning, and predominantly market-oriented questions, which summon the interlocutor primarily as an engagement metric — most statements, however, combine both logics in varying proportions. The results also reveal relevant differences between platforms: on Instagram, shaped by reels and carousels, the question tends to operate as a device for rapid identification and retention; on Facebook, sustained by a more extensive commenting culture and by sharing across timelines and groups, it favors personal narrative and a sense of co-authorship. The study concludes that the digital question constitutes a technodiscursive practice whose effectiveness stems from the articulation between language, interface, algorithms, and social participation, with relevant implications for critical literacy and for the teaching of Portuguese Language.

items.title: Interpreting isiZulu Idioms with Large Language Models: A Comparative Study of Zero-Shot Prompting, Retrieval-Augmented Generation, and Supervised Fine-Tuning
items.abstract: Idiom interpretation requires cultural knowledge, context, and pragmatic understanding that cannot be inferred from literal word meanings alone. This challenge is particularly important for isiZulu, a richly inflected Nguni Bantu language with limited representation in the web-scale corpora used to train modern large language models (LLMs). We compare three approaches to isiZulu idiom interpretation (zero-shot prompting, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) with glossary evidence, and supervised fine-tuning on a purpose-built, context-rich corpus) across five open-weight LLMs, evaluating them on 323 held-out idioms. Performance is evaluated using automated metrics and human assessment by expert isiZulu speakers. Supervised fine-tuning provides the strongest overall improvement, increasing the mean human evaluation score from 2.61 to 3.68 out of 5. RAG also improves interpretation quality, although its gains are smaller and are not fully captured by conventional surface-level metrics. Across the fifteen model--condition systems, COMET aligns best with human assessment, whereas embedding cosine similarity is the only metric that does not align positively with it, suggesting that this metric should be validated against human judgement before being used to evaluate idiomatic interpretation in low-resource languages. We contribute the isiZulu Idiom Dataset, a morphology-aware retrieval pipeline, and a reusable protocol for evaluating LLM-based idiom interpretation in low-resource African languages.

items.title: IRIS: Intelligent Real-Time Information System - A Voice-First, On-Device Android Assistant for Visually Impaired Users
items.abstract: This paper presents IRIS, an Intelligent Real-Time Informa-tion System: a voice-first Android assistant designed to give visually impaired people real-time awareness of their surroundings. Visually impaired people mostly rely on white canes, Braille and screen readers, which detect only nearby obstacles or work only with prepared con-tent, while existing smart-glasses and single-purpose applications are expensive, hardware-dependent and scattered across many tools. To address this issue, the proposed system combines scene description, text reading, currency identification, recognition of familiar faces, ob-stacle alerts, spoken navigation and SOS alerts in a single smartphone application. A four-layer architecture, consisting of a user interface layer, an application logic layer, a core modules layer and a hardware layer, runs the core artificial intelligence on the device, with a command router linking the speech, vision, emergency and navigation services. Audio and haptic feedback make the system hands-free and real-time, while an SOS command sends an SMS with the live location and calls a caretaker. The system is therefore low-cost, accessible and runs on an ordinary smartphone. This paper presents the literature survey, problem identification, proposed system, system requirements and system design of IRIS

items.title: Juridical Questions in Heterogeneous Relational Systems: A Discussion Paper
items.abstract: This discussion paper considers selected questions that arise when juridical processes concern heterogeneous subjects and systems whose histories, dynamics, manifestations, and institutional positions differ. Causal and informational coupling can coexist with distinct interpretive frameworks: culturally differentiated human communities, human–AI arrangements, and human relationships with terrestrial animals and ecosystems can be interdependent while possessing different capacities, temporal scales, and evidentiary categories. The paper revisits seven interacting concerns examined in an earlier study of nonlinear juridical processes: critical transitions, historical dependence, distributed causation, partial observability, situated interpretation, reflexive intervention, and irreversibility. It asks how heterogeneity may modify their significance for particular juridical functions. A further question concerns the recognition of juridically relevant subjects, considered through distinct inquiries into moral consideration, legal personality, standing, representation, and responsibility. The paper develops a provisional comparative vocabulary and considers four settings: culturally differentiated human communities, human–AI administrative processes, terrestrial interspecies relations, and a hypothetical first-contact case. Existing legal materials, including selected human-rights, environmental, animal-welfare, and AI-governance instruments, provide selected illustrations for the comparative inquiry. items.title: Large Language Models Are Not Interchangeable for Empiric Antibiotic Recommendations Under a Stewardship Benchmark: A Paired Retrospective Multi-Model Study
items.abstract: Background/Objectives: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly evaluated for empiric antibiotic decision support, but it remains unclear whether contemporary systems behave similarly under the same clinical and stewardship constraints. We compared four LLM configurations on real internal medicine admissions using a common, auditable stewardship benchmark. Methods: This single-center, retrospective, paired, non-interventional shadow-mode study included 486 admissions from a previously published 493-admission internal medicine cohort. For each admission, the clinician-prescribed empiric regimen was compared with recommendations from OpenAI GPT-5.5, Anthropic Claude Opus 4.7, Google Gemini 2.5 Pro, and Mistral Large 2512; OpenAI GPT-5.2 was analyzed separately as a supplementary legacy bridge. All LLMs received identical clinical content, local epidemiology context, antibiotic ontology, and three-field output schema. The primary endpoint was any contextually unsupported broad-spectrum escalation, defined by the study’s prespecified guardrail rules; the key secondary endpoint was a weighted contextual escalation penalty. Results: Clinician regimens met the primary endpoint in 16.7% of admissions. Rates were 13.0% for GPT-5.5 (paired risk difference [RD] −3.7 percentage points; Holm-adjusted p = 0.216), 15.0% for Gemini 2.5 Pro (RD −1.6; Holm-adjusted p = 0.509), 29.8% for Claude Opus 4.7 (RD +13.2; Holm-adjusted p < 0.001), and 31.9% for Mistral Large 2512 (RD +15.2; Holm-adjusted p < 0.001). Mean weighted contextual escalation penalty was 0.288 for clinician prescribing, 0.173 for GPT-5.5, 0.165 for Gemini, 0.510 for Claude, and 0.348 for Mistral. Global heterogeneity across contemporary LLMs was significant for both endpoints (p < 0.001). Conclusions: Contemporary LLM configurations were not interchangeable under the same stewardship benchmark. The benchmark measures stewardship-process performance (contextually unsupported escalation), not microbiological adequacy or missed coverage; fewer violations should therefore not be read as better overall therapy. These findings support configuration-specific, version-locked local evaluation before prospective shadow-mode and human-in-the-loop assessment.

items.title: Large language models facilitate knowledge extraction for troubleshooting
items.abstract: Troubleshooting in operational environments relies on expert knowledge that is often undocumented and highly contextual. Informal data sources, such as communication logs, may hold some of this information, but their unstructured nature makes interpretation challenging. In a preliminary case study with a telescope operations facility, we explored whether large language models (LLMs) can reconstruct troubleshooting strategies from chat logs. LLM outputs were compared against those produced by a novice human analyst by two expert evaluators. We also compared an LLM with additional technical information in the context window and LLM outputs augmented by another novice analyst. While the domain experts varied in their scoring, overall LLM-generated analyses were judged as higher quality and more accurate than human-produced outputs. Neither additional technical context nor human augmentation resulted in meaningful improvements. These preliminary findings suggest LLMs show promise for expert knowledge extraction and decision-support in operational environments.

items.title: Large Language Models for Multi-Lingual Equivalent Mutant Detection: An Extended Empirical Study
items.abstract: Mutation testing is a powerful technique for ensuring software quality. However, the presence of equivalent mutants introduces unnecessary costs and biases, limiting its practical effectiveness. Although numerous equivalent mutant detection (EMD) methods have been proposed, they often face distinct challenges: pure-code analysis methods can be limited by their reliance on specific compiler infrastructures, while existing machine-learning approaches remain constrained by scarce training data and limited generalization to unseen mutants. Large language models (LLMs) have recently demonstrated remarkable performance across diverse code-related tasks by better capturing program semantics. Yet their potential for EMD remains largely unexplored, particularly in the multi-lingual context. This paper presents the first comprehensive empirical study on LLMs for EMD, using 3,302 Java and 1,088 C mutant pairs to benchmark against state-of-the-art methods, explore strategy variations, assess efficiency, and evaluate cross-lingual generalization. Experimental results show that LLM-based approaches achieve higher F1-scores than the evaluated traditional methods, with fine-tuned code embedding yielding the highest detection accuracy among the tested strategies. Moreover, LLM-based approaches strike a practical balance between effectiveness and efficiency with inference times comparable to existing machine-learning models. Importantly, fine-tuned LLMs demonstrate measurable generalization across programming languages. These findings establish LLMs as a viable and efficient approach for tackling the longstanding challenge of equivalent mutant detection, offering new directions for advancing mutation testing in practice.
